evidence: Catull. 13.3–4: sī tēcum attuleris bonam atque magnam cēnam
Plin. Ep. 4.30.1: attulī tibi ex patriā meā prō mūnusculō quaestiōnem
terms.comment: Of things that are carried; people and animals, who walk, are brought with addūcō (Lewis & Short). Also spelled adferō. “Bring me …” is affer mihi ….

evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.21.5: quōs sēcum … Cratippus addūxit
terms.comment: sēcum addūcere, to bring someone along. Plautus and Terence also have the imperative addūce for addūc (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Attulī hunc. — Quid, attulistī? — Addūxī voluī dīcere.
phrases.english: I’ve carried him here. — What, carried him? — Brought him, I meant to say.

phrases.latin: sī tēcum attuleris bonam atque magnam cēnam
phrases.english: if you bring a good big dinner with you

phrases.latin: attulī tibi ex patriā meā prō mūnusculō quaestiōnem
phrases.english: I’ve brought you a little present from my home town: a puzzle
if you’ve got anything nice, bring it out
